junction.name: Frederick Douglass Boulevard & West 145 Street, New York City

claims.text: Frederick Douglass Boulevard & West 145 Street had 84 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 34 pedestrians injured, 21 cyclists injured and 0 people killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $5.8 million a year.
14% of crashes here had “other vehicular” recorded as a contributing factor, against 4% at the city's priority junctions.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: worked (pedestrian injury crashes changed -17% (95% interval -22% to -11%) at 1,651 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing).
The city's turn traffic calming: earlier trend (a simple before/after says -26%, but a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the decline cannot be credited to the program).
The city's enhanced crossings: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-7%, 95% interval -50% to +69%) could be zero).
The city's speed humps: not shown (at 1,008 sites the change in injury crashes (+0%, 95% interval -9% to +9%) could be zero).
Yellow Change Intervals would avoid about 4.6 crashes a year (CMF 4215, the median of 4 eligible records), worth $1.6 million a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.
Crosswalk Visibility Enhancements would avoid about 2.5 crashes a year (CMF 2697, the only eligible record), worth $861,000 a year; check on site: the crossings are not already high-visibility.
The NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is responsible for Frederick Douglass Boulevard, West 145 Street (not listed in NYSDOT Roadway Inventory, so a city street).
Who can push for it: Council Member, District 9, New York City Council; Manhattan Community Board 10.
A request letter to the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is drafted and checked.

draft_request.letter:
To: the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT)
Cc: Council Member, District 9, New York City Council; Manhattan Community Board 10
Subject: Request for safety study at Frederick Douglass Boulevard & West 145 Street

Dear colleagues at NYC DOT,

We are writing to ask you to complete a safety study at Frederick Douglass Boulevard & West 145 Street, on the roads you are responsible for (Frederick Douglass Boulevard and West 145 Street), and to make the fixes listed below that you find are needed after a site check.

The official record for the 5 years from 31 October 2021 shows 178 crashes, including 84 injury crashes. In that time 34 pedestrians and 21 cyclists were injured and no people were killed. This junction is a city priority location. No safety work is recorded in this period, with the latest recorded project a Leading Pedestrian Interval signal in 2018. Using the U.S. DOT's official values for the cost of crashes (2024 dollars), the yearly cost of the harm here is $5.8 million.

Please consider these low-cost fixes:

- longer yellow signal times (Yellow Change Intervals): expected to prevent about 4.6 injury crashes per year, avoiding about $1,565,000 in harm per year. Please check on site for an entry on yellow or red first. It would pay for itself if it costs under $11.0 million.

- high-visibility crosswalks (Crosswalk Visibility Enhancements): expected to prevent about 2.5 pedestrian injury crashes per year, avoiding about $861,000 in harm per year. Please check that the crossings are not already high-visibility. It would pay for itself if it costs under $6.1 million.

Thank you for your work to make our streets safer.

[Your name]
[Your organisation or address]
